follow-up time: Early pregnancy to discharge after birth
exposure: Lifestyle interventions (diet, physical activity and/or behavioural)
cohort: Pregnant women receiving routine antenatal care in secondary and tertiary care hospitals in Australia
finding: Lifestyle interventions during pregnancy were likely cost-effective in reducing the risk of gestational diabetes and/or hypertensive disease in pregnancy.
mod_finding: This study found that lifestyle interventions during pregnancy were cost-effective in reducing the risk of gestational diabetes and hypertensive disorders, which are associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean section.
